nodes.label: Risk assessment and strategies
nodes.title: Base the emergency plan on documented facility-based and community-based risk assessments using an all-hazards approach, including missing residents, and include strategies for identified events.

nodes.label: Population needs and continuity
nodes.title: Address resident population needs, services the facility can provide during emergencies, and continuity of operations including delegations of authority and succession plans.

nodes.label: Collaboration with officials
nodes.title: Include a documented process for cooperation and collaboration with emergency preparedness officials and integrated planning partners.

nodes.label: Policies and procedures
nodes.title: Develop and implement emergency preparedness policies and procedures based on the emergency plan, risk assessment, and communication plan, and review them annually.

nodes.label: Subsistence and utilities
nodes.title: Provide for subsistence needs during evacuation or shelter-in-place, including food, water, medical supplies, alternate energy, emergency lighting, fire systems, and sewage and waste disposal.

nodes.label: Emergency operations
nodes.title: Maintain operational policies for evacuation, sheltering, resident tracking, medical documentation, staffing and volunteers, transfer arrangements, and other emergency operating procedures required for LTC response.

nodes.label: 1135 waiver alternate care site
nodes.title: Address the facility role under an 1135 waiver when emergency management officials identify an alternate care site for emergency resident care.

nodes.label: Communication plan
nodes.title: Maintain an emergency preparedness communication plan that complies with law and is reviewed and updated annually.

nodes.label: Contact information
nodes.title: Maintain current contact information for staff, physicians, other facilities, residents' representatives, and other contacts required to support emergency communication.

nodes.label: Agency contacts
nodes.title: Maintain contact information for emergency preparedness staff, the state licensing and certification agency, the state long-term care ombudsman, and other sources of assistance.

nodes.label: Primary and alternate communications
nodes.title: Provide primary and alternate means of communication with staff and emergency management agencies.

nodes.label: Information sharing
nodes.title: Share resident information and medical documentation to maintain continuity of care, release information as permitted, provide condition and location updates, and report occupancy, needs, and ability to assist.

nodes.label: Resident and family sharing
nodes.title: Use an appropriate method to share emergency plan information with residents and their families or representatives.

nodes.label: Training and testing program
nodes.title: Maintain an annual emergency preparedness training and testing program tied to the emergency plan, risk assessment, policies, and communication plan.

nodes.label: Staff training
nodes.title: Provide initial and annual emergency preparedness training, maintain documentation, and demonstrate staff knowledge of emergency procedures.

nodes.label: Exercises and testing
nodes.title: Conduct annual exercises, including unannounced staff drills, document performance, analyze results, and revise the emergency plan as needed.

nodes.label: Emergency power systems
nodes.title: Implement emergency and standby power systems, including compliant generator location, inspection, testing, and fuel planning when applicable.

nodes.label: Integrated health system program
nodes.title: If the facility elects to participate in a unified healthcare system emergency preparedness program, the integrated program must document facility participation, facility-specific risk assessment, coordinated communications, and coordinated training and testing.

nodes.label: Emergency preparedness program
nodes.title: Maintain a comprehensive, all-hazards emergency preparedness program that complies with applicable federal, state, and local requirements and is reviewed annually.
